夏卡爾（Marc Chagall，1887-1985）一位情感豐富、浪漫的畫家和詩人。出生於俄羅斯一個卑微保守的猶太農村家庭（維台普斯克, Vitsyebsk )，他一生經歷了俄國革命以及兩次世界大戰，戰火再加上他的猶太人身份，在在讓他感受到世事的變動難測，以及自己與生俱來的文化宿命。種種起伏翻動的情感都在他的畫作中呈現出來。除了故鄉、猶太文化與愛情之外，夏卡爾一生還創作做出了許多如夢般的畫作。進入夏卡爾的畫，彷彿走進夢幻世界。他將事物以幽默，幻想及無意識的方式處理，使作品藴含着詩意和另一層次的美學。以他創作的内容和走向，藝術史學家們將他歸納在超現實主義 (Surrealism) 或「超自然」風格中。但也有人認為他獨特的繪畫風格並不屬於任何派別，他只屬於他自己。
圖1：《 The Birthday 》 1915。    Museum of Modern Art    New York
除了繪畫之外，夏卡爾為人所熟知的，是他豐富的感情生活。除了年輕時候的種種感情外，他一生中最摯愛的，莫過於第一任妻子貝拉（Bella）。為了貝拉，夏卡爾創作出三十多幅畫作，畫作表達出他對於貝拉真摯長流的情感。「她翱翔在我的畫布上已有多年，引領我的創作。」夏卡爾這麼說。 在藝術史中，以單純男女情愛為主題的畫家可以說屈指可數，但夏卡爾卻畫出了以他與妻子-貝拉之間的深情畫作，以夏卡爾在藝術史中的地位，加上畫作中的夢幻情懷，夏卡爾無疑的是位浪漫和感情真摰的藝術家。
圖2：《 I and the village》 1911。    Museum of Modern Art    New York
記憶中的紛繁影像有如萬花筒般，在這幅描繪家鄉維特巴斯克的畫裏一起出現。雖然夏卡爾一生中在故鄉只待過短短幾年，但這些日子的影像，卻深深烙印在他的腦海裡，他以繪畫來表達家鄉以及俄國農村在他内心的懷念和眷戀，在許多其他作品中，也經常出現有農村景象，牛，馬，鷄和鴿子等繪畫，可見家鄉俄國對他有多大的牽繫。
points.en:
I walk to where the water ends, and sit and watch the clouds rise.
By chance I meet an old woodsman of the forest; we talk and laugh, with no fixed time to part.
-- Tang Dynasty. Wang Wei, "My Retreat at Mount Zhongnan"
Marc Chagall (1887–1985) was a deeply emotional and romantic painter and poet. Born into a humble, traditional Jewish farming family in Vitebsk, Russia, he lived through the Russian Revolution and two world wars; the turmoil of war, compounded by his Jewish identity, gave him a keen sense of the unpredictability of worldly affairs and of his own inborn cultural destiny. All these swirling, shifting emotions found expression in his paintings. Beyond his homeland, Jewish culture, and love, Chagall produced throughout his life many dreamlike paintings. Entering a Chagall painting feels like stepping into a fantastical world. He treated things with humor, fantasy, and an unconscious quality, giving his works a poetic sensibility and another layer of aesthetic meaning. Given the content and direction of his work, art historians classify him within Surrealism or a "supernatural" style. Yet others feel his distinctive painting style belongs to no school at all — he belongs only to himself.
Figure 1: "The Birthday," 1915. Museum of Modern Art, New York.
Beyond painting, Chagall is well known for his rich emotional life. Apart from his various romances in his youth, the great love of his life was undoubtedly his first wife, Bella. For Bella, Chagall created more than thirty paintings expressing his sincere, enduring feelings for her. "She has soared above my canvases for years, guiding my creation," Chagall said. In art history, painters who take pure romantic love between a man and a woman as their central subject can be counted on one hand, yet Chagall painted deeply loving works centered on himself and his wife Bella; given Chagall's stature in art history combined with the dreamlike sentiment in these paintings, he is undoubtedly a romantic and deeply sincere artist.
Figure 2: "I and the Village," 1911. Museum of Modern Art, New York.
The kaleidoscope of memories all appear together in this painting depicting his hometown of Vitebsk. Although Chagall spent only a few short years of his life in his hometown, the images of those days were deeply etched in his mind; he used painting to express the nostalgia and longing he felt in his heart for his hometown and the Russian countryside. In many of his other works, scenes of rural life, cows, horses, chickens, and pigeons often appear as well, showing just how strong his ties to his Russian homeland were.

en: Grass sprouts, its color swaying in the wind
The wind blows through March's cherry blossoms
Toward evening, I copied down a few lines of a poet's verse
Below the southern hills, beside the bamboo fence
Cutting a few more sprigs of autumn chrysanthemum

points.zh:
結廬在人境，而無車馬喧。
問君何能爾，心遠地自偏。
採菊東籬下，悠然見南山。
山氣日夕佳，飛鳥相與還。
此中有真意，欲辨已忘言。
--東晉。 陶淵明《 飲酒   其五》
points.en:
I built my hut amid the world of men, yet there is no noise of carriages or horses.
You ask how this can be — when the heart is far, the place itself becomes remote.
I pick chrysanthemums under the eastern hedge, and in the distance calmly see the southern mountain.
The mountain air is beautiful at dusk, as birds fly home together in flocks.
In all this there is a true meaning — I wish to explain it, but have already forgotten the words.
-- Eastern Jin. Tao Yuanming, 'Drinking Wine, No. 5'

points.zh:
Are you really just a pile of genes?  Technically, yes. But embedded within your genome
there are many potential versions of you. The person you see in the mirror is just one of them,
fished out by the unique things you’ve exposed to since conception. The new science of epigenetics is the study of how chemical changes made to DNA, or proteins that interact with DNA, can affect gene activity. DNA can be modified by environmental factors in ways that can profoundly affect development and behavior. Recently, it’s also been shown that microbes in your body – aka your microbiome – can be a significant environmental factor that affect myriad behaviors, from overeating to depression. In sum, we are our genes – but our genes cannot be evaluated outside the context of our environment. Gens are the piano keys, but the environment plays the song.  – BS.           --National Geographic   September 2019
《 The Sound of Silence 》
Song composer:  Paul Simon,  1966
Hello darkness, my old friend
I've come to talk with you again
Because a vision softly creeping
Left its seeds while I was sleeping
And the vision that was planted in my brain
Still remains
Within the sound of silence
And in the naked light I saw
Ten thousand people, maybe more
People talking without speaking
People hearing without listening
People writing songs that voices never share
And no one dared
Disturb the sound of silence
